newsitem.title: DENMARK: FLS, SAS take Danish shares to new heights.
newsitem.headline: FLS, SAS take Danish shares to new heights.

text.p: Danish share prices, intoxicated by the strong dollar like markets around Europe, stormed to a new high on Thursday for the 13th time this month and dealers saw nothing likely to prevent further gains.
"The underlying factors favour further rises and if the dollar and the Dow Jones deliver again there could be another rise in Friday," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 5.23 point to 195.61 -- a 2.75 percent rise -- in overall bourse turnover of 1.80 billion crowns. Its August future rose 4.25 point to 195.75 with 909 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Cement and engineering group FLS led the charge, with a 10 percent rise to 265.00 crowns, a surge for which dealers could offer no explanation.

Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) scored a 7.78 percent advance to 97.00 crowns, ascribed variously to increased passenger volume figures from Copenhagen Airports, buy recommendations from London analysts and an unidentified major buyer on the local market.
NatWest described the paper vas Europe's most undervalued aviation share and predicted that the stock would rise a further 40 percent over the coming 12 months. REUTER
